Theme: Older adults accept family involvement when they stay in control
Organizing concept: Older adults accept family involvement when the agent explains it, lets them respond first, allows refusal, and keeps medicine decisions with people.
Sub-theme: Older adults respond before family is involved
What it means: The agent explains family involvement, reminds the older adult first, waits, and contacts only one chosen person when needed.
Boundary and variation: Risk graded veto weakening was not deployed; repeated requests can become irritating.
RQ and contribution: RQ2 and RQ3; direction, visibility, revocability, and ceremony; C2 and C3

Theme: Older adults accept family involvement when they stay in control
Organizing concept: Older adults accept family involvement when the agent explains it, lets them respond first, allows refusal, and keeps medicine decisions with people.
Sub-theme: People check before trusting the agent
What it means: People compare the agent with prescriptions and known routines, refuse errors, and return to familiar methods when needed.
Boundary and variation: The agent cannot establish ingestion, prescribe, or change medicine.
RQ and contribution: RQ2 and RQ3; tool and advocate boundaries; C2 and C3

Theme: Routines and prescriptions matter more than scores and streaks
Organizing concept: Routines and prescriptions drive medication taking; streaks add small interest but can also cause disappointment and pressure.
Sub-theme: Routines and prescriptions come before scores
What it means: Long-term routines and doctors' instructions make medicine necessary before game feedback appears.
Boundary and variation: Some older adults find scores unnecessary or difficult to understand.
RQ and contribution: RQ3; motivation and coach-role boundary; C3

Theme: Routines and prescriptions matter more than scores and streaks
Organizing concept: Routines and prescriptions drive medication taking; streaks add small interest but can also cause disappointment and pressure.
Sub-theme: A streak can add small interest
What it means: A streak can show regular practice and make that effort visible to family.
Boundary and variation: No younger comparison group exists, and no adherence effect can be inferred.

Theme: Routines and prescriptions matter more than scores and streaks
Organizing concept: Routines and prescriptions drive medication taking; streaks add small interest but can also cause disappointment and pressure.
What it means: Losing a streak can cause disappointment, while family can return attention to the next medicine event.
Boundary and variation: Monitoring, competition, performance judgment, and score anxiety can make the feature unacceptable.

Theme: Friends and community shape care, but doctors decide medicine
Organizing concept: Older adults remind others and learn from friends and community groups, while doctors retain authority and digital sharing stays optional.
Sub-theme: People remind and learn from each other
What it means: Mutual reminders and everyday medicine talk let older adults care for others and receive reminders themselves.
Boundary and variation: Community questions appeared only in a subset and were mostly elicited.
RQ and contribution: RQ2 and RQ3; extended care network; C2

Theme: Friends and community shape care, but doctors decide medicine
Organizing concept: Older adults remind others and learn from friends and community groups, while doctors retain authority and digital sharing stays optional.
Sub-theme: Community advice leads to questions, not decisions
What it means: Community experience can build technology trust and raise questions, but doctors remain responsible for medicine decisions.
Boundary and variation: Peer talk can confuse, and conversational sharing does not authorize automatic digital disclosure.
RQ and contribution: RQ2 and RQ3; differentiated authority; C2 and C3

Theme: Care tasks are divided while older adults stay involved
Organizing concept: Family members can handle setup and supplies while older adults remain involved in taking, confirming, and checking medicine.
Sub-theme: Family setup can preserve older adult control
What it means: Relatives may set schedules while older adults take medicine, confirm doses, question errors, and refuse prompts.
Boundary and variation: Invisible changes or unavailable family helpers can turn assistance into dependence.
RQ and contribution: RQ2 and RQ3; direction and dignity; C2 and C3

Theme: Care tasks are divided while older adults stay involved
Organizing concept: Family members can handle setup and supplies while older adults remain involved in taking, confirming, and checking medicine.
Sub-theme: Features send tasks to responsible people
What it means: Stock alerts can reach the buyer, while prescription capture would still require checking by family, pharmacists, or doctors.
Boundary and variation: Stock sensing and prescription capture were not deployed.

Theme: The agent helps when it supports routines and shows uncertainty
Organizing concept: The agent supports rather than replaces older adults when it reinforces familiar routines, stays easy to use, and treats missing confirmation as uncertainty.
Sub-theme: Reminders can strengthen an existing routine
What it means: Portable reminders support changed routines and can make dose times easier to anticipate without replacing existing practices.
Boundary and variation: No logs or health outcomes establish adherence or cognitive improvement.
RQ and contribution: RQ3; prototype fit and cross-phase correction; C3

Theme: The agent helps when it supports routines and shows uncertainty
Organizing concept: The agent supports rather than replaces older adults when it reinforces familiar routines, stays easy to use, and treats missing confirmation as uncertainty.
What it means: Clear timing, Bangla speech, large text, medicine images, and few controls help older adults understand and respond.
Boundary and variation: Spoken service announcements were deployed; medicine images and selectable reminder modes were not.
RQ and contribution: RQ3; prototype evaluation and accessible interaction; C3

Theme: The agent helps when it supports routines and shows uncertainty
Organizing concept: The agent supports rather than replaces older adults when it reinforces familiar routines, stays easy to use, and treats missing confirmation as uncertainty.
Sub-theme: A missing response does not prove a missed dose
What it means: A missing response leads to a check because an older adult may take medicine without pressing the button.
Boundary and variation: False alerts can produce unnecessary worry; patterned silence interpretation was not deployed.
RQ and contribution: RQ2 and RQ3; implementation gap and contestability; C2 and C3
